key.name: check-interval-minutes
key.description: How often to run the update checks, in minutes.

key.name: notify-on-new
key.description: Show a desktop notification when the total update count goes up.

key.name: show-zero
key.summary: Keep the panel icon visible when up to date
key.description: By default the icon only appears in the panel when there's at least one update pending. Enable this to keep it visible (with a "0") even when everything is up to date.

key.name: sources
key.description: List of "Name|shell command" entries, editable from the preferences window. Each command runs through /bin/sh -c and its stdout is captured; the number of non-empty lines printed is treated as that source's update count. Add one entry per package manager you want tracked (cargo, npm, pipx, uv, etc.) - see the README for ready-made command snippets.

key.name: update-script-path
key.description: Path to a script (e.g. your fish update script) to run when "Run Update Script" is clicked in the menu. Leave empty to disable.

key.name: check-reboot-required
key.summary: Check whether a reboot is required
key.description: Shows a separate icon when the system needs a reboot to finish applying updates (e.g. after a kernel or glibc update).

key.name: source-update-commands
key.default: ['DNF|doas dnf update --refresh -y && doas dnf autoremove -y', 'Flatpak|flatpak update -y && flatpak uninstall --unused -y']
key.description: List of "Name|shell command" entries, matched by name against the "sources" list. When a source has updates AND a matching entry here, clicking it in the panel menu opens a terminal and runs this command - so you can update just that one thing instead of everything. Optional per source; a source with no matching entry just shows its count with no click action.

key.name: background-updates
key.summary: Run per-source updates in the background, no terminal
key.description: When enabled, clicking a source's update in the panel menu runs it in the background instead of opening a terminal. Any "doas"/"sudo" in the command is stripped and the whole command is re-run through pkexec, which shows a graphical password prompt instead. A notification reports success or failure. This only affects per-source update commands, not "Run Update Script" - an external script's contents can't be safely rewritten this way.

key.name: reboot-check-command
key.default: 'err=$(dnf needs-restarting -r 2>&1 1>/dev/null); code=$?; if [ "$code" = "1" ]; then echo "Reboot required to finish pending updates"; elif [ "$code" != "0" ]; then printf "%s\n" "$err" >&2; exit 1; fi'
key.description: A shell command that prints something on stdout if (and only if) a reboot is required, and nothing otherwise - matching how update sources are evaluated. The default wraps `dnf needs-restarting -r`, checking specifically for its documented exit code 1 ("reboot needed"); any other non-zero exit is treated as a real command failure, not a reboot signal, and surfaces via stderr like any other source error instead of being misread as "needed".

key.name: terminal-command
key.description: Command prefix used to open a terminal to run the update script interactively (so password prompts work). Adjust if you don't use GNOME Terminal, e.g. 'kgx --' or 'konsole -e'.
